Amsterdam, Netherlands; European and worldwide delivery

Business contact

Published shop email: hello@fussypeople.eu. General contact and delivery questions use the same address: https://www.fussypeople.eu/pages/faq .

Published operating context

The Shopify storefront sells vintage furniture and contemporary designs. It shows new arrivals and a sold archive; the shop also sources replacement stock across Europe. The delivery guide covers Belgium, wider Europe and overseas freight, with quotes for larger pieces.

Current language setup
Reviewed home, product and FAQ pages use English. Confirm any additional live languages with the shop.

A useful pilot is one newly listed item in French or German, carrying over designer names, dimensions, condition notes and the correct shipping-quote instructions. Review its product text, URL and search description, then change one source detail to check the update. Current pages were read in English; ask which other storefront languages and translation apps are already in use. Keep the existing catalog and shipping process.

Your new-arrivals catalog and EU delivery service make a focused language demo possible: one furniture listing, its condition notes and its shipping-quote instructions in French or German. Would a side-by-side review against your current storefront be useful?

    Shopify footer, Amsterdam location, published email, new arrivals and sourcing.

A partner prospect for spreadsheet conversion

Five additional distinct profiles are prepared for US$20 total, with the same research detail and an editable CSV. One correction or replacement is included within seven days for an existing customer, duplicate, dead published contact or clear mismatch.

Partner prospect 1

SmoothWork

Budapest, Hungary; remote clients across markets

https://smoothwork.ai/

Published business contact
hello@smoothwork.ai

Published business email hello@smoothwork.ai; +36 30 367 9742. The service page names Milan as its automation and Airtable consultant and lists 1053 Budapest, Ferenciek Square 2.

Existing service and workflow

SmoothWork explicitly offers API integrations that collect data and build reports, alongside code and no-code workflows, Airtable implementations and ongoing support. Its own n8n guide covers authenticated HTTP requests and JSON responses.

Tools already in use

Custom API integrations, n8n HTTP requests, Airtable and code/no-code client workflows already exist. The reviewed sources do not identify its current XLSX generation component.

Suggested JSON Support comparison

Offer a short comparison for one existing API-to-spreadsheet report: post an approved small JSON response to JSON Support, receive the XLSX and compare column expansion, dates, numbers and file handoff with SmoothWork's current implementation. For recurring client delivery, compare the Pro inbound webhook's emailed workbook with the existing n8n or scripted delivery step. Keep data preparation and client-specific business logic in SmoothWork's existing workflow.

Suggested opening
Your API integration service already covers collecting data and building reports, and your n8n guide walks through authenticated JSON requests. Would a small JSON-to-XLSX comparison be useful for a client workflow where the last step is delivering a spreadsheet? We can compare it with the component you already use.
Qualify the workflow

Confirm the present workbook-generation method, typical payload size, nested-array layout, destination and monthly call volume. Use an approved non-sensitive example first. The authenticated API processes data on the server; the separate free browser converter runs locally. Confirm current API limits and whether clients permit that service before choosing it.

Original sources
  • https://smoothwork.ai/custom-api-integration-services/
    API data collection and reporting service, code/no-code delivery, consultant Milan and public email/phone/Budapest contact.
  • https://smoothwork.ai/connect_to_any_apis_in_n8n/
    Published authenticated n8n HTTP-request and JSON workflow.

How to use these introductions

Begin with the prospect’s existing conversion method and a small approved example. Compare actual headers, values, nested-record layout and the required handoff. Keep client-specific formulas, macros, reconciliation and report design in the existing system.

The free browser converter and the authenticated server API have different operating boundaries. For a recurring API or Pro webhook use, agree client data permissions, current size and usage limits, destination and recurring cost before a pilot.

This course selects the exact free and paid HTMLs for Unlost, MapRank, JSON Support, HoundStack and Pool Pro from their retained current sources.
